interface.title: ASMS Project Compound Pooling Panels (ASMS Pooling Calculator)
interface.field: Medicinal chemistry / high-throughput screening (affinity-selection mass spectrometry, HRMS)
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment design and plate preparation before an AS-MS screen, plus reconciliation after the liquid-handler run (the post-run reconciliation tabs were not reached in this run)
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn a compound library SDF into mass-diverse 384-well source pools sorted by ionization polarity, map those pools onto 96-well assay plates, and export manifests, Echo picklists and an interactive plate map.

data.note: The run used mini_library.sdf (8 records: 7 parsed, 1 corrupted record left out) with plate prefix ASMS_TEST and later ASMS_RUN2. I also uploaded optional_1536_master_map.csv as the 1536 master map. It gave '0 Match IDs Identified', so no consolidation picklist was made. The map has an NCGC_ID column. The mismatch came from the test SDF: the app reads each record's title line (_Name) before SAMPLE_ID (app.py:366), and mini_library.sdf's titles are compound names such as 'Benzylamine', so its NCGC IDs were never used. Tabs 2–4 need inputs that this run did not have: a 2D visual plate-map xlsx, an Echo volume survey, and an Echo exception report with a source manifest. Small synthetic versions could be built. Files the app downloads cannot be uploaded back into it through the browser agent.

features.name: Polarity-split, mass-stride pooling engine
features.general: Give each item a detection mode from chemical-group rules, then within each mode sort by mass-to-charge and deal items across pools by stride, so co-pooled items are far apart in mass and each pool uses one detection mode
features.specific: Ionization polarity is predicted from SMARTS rules. Compounds are sorted by Target_m_z within each polarity and distributed across wells by stride, and negative-mode pools are placed before positive-mode ones. Here A01 held the acid and acetate at −1.007, and A02 held the amines and glycine at +1.007. At 2 per well, the duplicate benzylamine lots were split into separate wells. No polarity column is shown; mode is read from the sign of Target_m_z − Exact_Mass
steps: Set Target Compounds per Well and the Δm/z threshold
Run the engine on the SDF
Read Target_m_z against Exact_Mass to see each well's polarity
Read Min_Δm/z_In_Well for the spread within each well
Change the pool size and see compounds redistributed across wells
serves_tasks: Check each item's assigned detection mode and confirm co-pooled items are far enough apart
Choose pool size and the minimum separation allowed between items in a pool

Duplicate-lot merging (app.py:528) was never exercised. Benzylamine and Benzylamine_Duplicate_Lot have different SDF titles, and titles take priority over SAMPLE_ID (app.py:366), so the app treated them as two compounds. This is a test-data problem, not an app fault. With 10 per well they shared a well at Δm/z 0; with 2 per well they were split

Confirmed code defect: a single-compound well gets Min_Δm/z_In_Well 0 because app.py:493 turns inf into 0.0, and app.py:581 counts it as below threshold. That is why the Mass Resolution Alert still flagged 1 well (the Aliniline-only well A04) at 2 per well
